validityReview.criteriaSource: CLAUDE.md C4 Known-Invalid / Out-of-Scope + Three-Law Hierarchy (Law 3 footgun exception)
validityReview.summary: All 6 findings are VALID. The two owner footgun findings (001, 002) survive Law-3 / KI#4 because each is a NON-OBVIOUS consequence that would surprise a competent, non-malicious owner and silently breaks a backing-integrity story (Law-2) / enables an unbacked-mint tail (Law-1); neither is a malicious-owner vector nor an obvious-harm misconfig. The MEV finding (L06) is a legitimate bounded value-leak Low, not a user-input mistake nor pure speculation. None of the findings rely on weird/FoT tokens, approve-race, CryptoPunks, future-code speculation, or unused-view-function patterns in an invalidating way. Source claims independently verified against Uniboost/ATokenDispatcherV2/UniboostMintDebtHook/DefaultDispatchHook.

findings.title: Uniboost no hookTypeId guard -> unwired hook accrues 0 phUSD debt

law3Test.question: Would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED by this consequence?
law3Test.reasoning: The dispatcher SILENTLY accepts dispatches with the constructor-default no-op DefaultDispatchHook (or a mismatched hook). There is no hookTypeId marker check on the dispatch path (verified ATokenDispatcherV2.sol:124-125 calls hook.onDispatch unconditionally; DefaultDispatchHook.onDispatch is an empty no-op at DefaultDispatchHook.sol:12). An owner who has correctly deployed two prior dispatchers and seen the M-04 NudgeRatchet FIXED with a hookTypeId guard would reasonably ASSUME the same guard exists here; its absence is non-obvious. The harm (Uniboost-routed prime accrues ZERO backing debt -> a backing-integrity story silently fails, Law-2) is invisible at deploy: no revert, no event, dispatch still functions. This is the inverse of an obvious misconfig (price=0, point-at-malicious-token) which a competent operator would immediately recognize.

findings.ki4Suppression: NOT suppressed. KI#4 (reckless admin mistake) covers owner malice or obvious-harm misconfig only. This is a non-obvious operational hazard surfaced with safe-config guidance, exactly the CLAUDE.md Law-3 in-scope exception. Q-08 (BalancerPoolerV2) is the same fail-open class but a DISTINCT contract/function -> distinct fingerprint -> NOT auto-suppressed by the Q-08 wont-fix; routed for explicit owner decision.
findings.verdict: VALID. Keep as Low operational hazard / owner footgun. Route for explicit owner accept/fix decision (do not auto-apply Q-08 wont-fix).

findings.title: UniboostMintDebtHook.scale decoupled from dispatcher primeToken() -> deploy-time mis-scale

checks.note: Decimal-awareness is a legitimate scale concern; not the weird-token / FoT exclusion. Decimal MATH correctness (d<=18) is guarded at ctor line 86 and explicitly NOT re-raised.

law3Test.question: Would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED by this consequence?
law3Test.reasoning: The ctor takes dispatcher_ and primeToken_ as two SEPARATE same-typed address args and derives the immutable scale = 10**(18 - primeToken_.decimals()) with NO on-chain tie to the dispatcher's actual prime (verified UniboostMintDebtHook.sol:81-89). The natural owner assumption, reinforced by the M-03/M-04 fix lineage that made the hook 'prime-decimals-aware', is that scale is bound to the dispatcher it serves. It is not. Passing a primeToken_ whose decimals differ from the dispatcher's real prime type-checks and silently bakes a wrong immutable scale. The over-scale direction mints UNBACKED phUSD on a later pull() (Law-1 tail) -> this is precisely a non-obvious owner action that unknowingly enables an exploit-class outcome, the textbook CLAUDE.md footgun. Not an obvious misconfig: both args are plausible addresses and nothing at deploy signals the mismatch.

findings.ki4Suppression: NOT suppressed. Same Law-3 in-scope footgun rationale as 001. The unbacked-over-mint tail is the Law-1 recall-keep justification; the absence of any external/runtime attacker keeps it at Low rather than escalating, but does NOT make it invalid.
findings.severityNote: Low is defensible (no external requirement, single atomic owner deploy error, detectable pre-pull). Validity is independent of the Low-vs-Medium debate; this agent confirms validity, not severity.
findings.verdict: VALID. Keep as Low deploy-config footgun with the ctor-assertion remediation (tie scale to dispatcher.primeToken()).

findings.title: setPool repoints _pairToken without re-validating stored _primeToPairPath

law3Test.question: Would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED that setPool does not re-validate the stored custom path?
law3Test.answer: Mildly YES -> QA-bundle note, not suppressed.
law3Test.reasoning: The setter silently breaks its own advertised path-end==pairToken invariant across setPool. Impact ceiling is LOUD (next pool() reverts/under-funds against on-chain minPairOut/minTargetOut floors; dust sweepable via rescueERC20). No silent value leak, so QA is the correct floor. A non-malicious owner could be surprised the stored path is not auto-cleared, so it is surfaced as a QA state-handling note rather than dropped under KI#1/KI#4.

findings.verdict: VALID as QA. Incorrect state-handling / invariant-break with loud, recoverable impact. Keep in QA bundle.

findings.title: Uniboost pool() buy-and-pool LP-add MEV (dedup to open L-06)

checks.note: Operator-set floors are not a 'user input mistake' phishing/typo pattern; this is a structural off-chain-min-only LP-add with an exploitable slack window. The MEV path requires a sandwicher (external actor), not a user error.
Root cause is present live code (off-chain min-only LP add with no on-chain TWAP/oracle reference), not speculation on future code.

findings.mevAssessment: Legitimate bounded value-leak-to-MEV Low. POL-only (protocol-owned liquidity), operator-triggered, bounded by keeper-supplied minPairOut/minTargetOut + post-call minLP. The exploitable surface is only the slack between the off-chain floor and true price. Same root-cause class as OPEN ledger L-06 (BalancerPoolerV2.pool). This is the canonical C4-valid 'value leak with external (MEV) requirement' shape; not an invalid user mistake and not speculation.

law3Test.note: Not an owner-footgun finding; external MEV actor required.

findings.verdict: VALID. Keep as Low; dedup to open L-06 as a cross-contract second instance.

findings.title: donationSplit <-> hook.ratio cross-contract decoupling (dedup to open L-05)

law3Test.question: Would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED that donationSplit (Uniboost) and ratio (hook) have no on-chain coupling invariant?
law3Test.answer: YES, mildly -> non-obvious transparency/coupling footgun, in scope at Low.
law3Test.reasoning: Two params on two different contracts with no on-chain invariant tying them; a mismatched pair is silently accepted. No solvency break: ratio is hard-capped at MAX_RATIO=50 (verified UniboostMintDebtHook.sol:31), so worst-case accrued debt is <=50% of dispatched prime against ~100% retained value at dispatch -> conservative backing buffer holds (Tier-3 confirms >=2:1). This is a non-obvious config-coupling gap, not a malicious-owner vector and not an obvious misconfig. Same class as OPEN ledger L-05.

findings.verdict: VALID. Keep as Low; dedup to open L-05 as a cross-contract second instance.

findings.title: setRatio accepts ==MAX_RATIO vs 'strictly <' NatSpec (dedup to L-02)
findings.specVsCode: Confirmed live: setRatio uses `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert` (UniboostMintDebtHook.sol:97), accepting ratio==50, contradicting the 'strictly less than MAX_RATIO' NatSpec (lines 30/55/95). This is a Law-2 documented-behavior deviation (faithfulness:true) with ZERO security impact (effective cap 50% vs <50%, both inside the >=2:1 buffer). A spec-vs-code boundary nit is QA-valid, NOT the invalid 'documentation gap presented as vulnerability' pattern, because it is surfaced honestly at QA via its faithfulness tag rather than inflated.
findings.verdict: VALID as QA. Keep in QA bundle + spec-conformance routing; dedup to L-02.

validityReview.recommendation: Proceed with all 6 findings. None dropped. Route 001 and 002 for explicit owner accept/fix decisions (do not auto-suppress 001 under Q-08). 002 carries an unbacked-mint Law-1 tail that mandates retention regardless of the Low-vs-Medium severity debate.
